title: Open Tree of Life web services

title: The origin and early radiation of dinosaurs
authors: Brusatte, S.L.; Nesbitt, S.J.; Irmis, R.B.; et al.

title: Extreme convergence in the body plans of an early suchian (Archosauria) and ornithomimid dinosaurs (Theropoda)
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: The nearly complete AMNH FR 30587 skeleton anchors the anatomical comparison; suchian placement and convergence are character-matrix interpretations, not ancestry or identical ecology.

title: Early crocodylomorph increases top tier predator diversity during rise of dinosaurs
authors: Zanno, L.E.; Drymala, S.; Nesbitt, S.J.; Schneider, V.P.
note: NCSM 21558 is a partial, skeletally immature holotype from the Carnian Pekin Formation; size, trophic role and topology are bounded interpretations.

title: A Middle Jurassic 'sphenosuchian' from China and the origin of the crocodylian skull
authors: Clark, J.M.; Xu, X.; Forster, C.A.; Wang, Y.
note: IVPP V14010 preserves an articulated anterior skeleton and nearly complete skull from the lower Shishugou Formation; skull consolidation and placement are comparative interpretations.

title: Tip-dating and homoplasy: reconciling the shallow molecular divergences of modern gharials with their long fossil record
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: The combined tip-dated analysis samples 117 taxa, 278 morphological characters and 9284 molecular base pairs; topology and times depend on model, priors and character treatment.

title: A well-preserved Archaeopteryx specimen with theropod features
authors: Mayr, G.; Pohl, B.; Peters, D.S.
note: The Thermopolis specimen, later catalogued WDC CSG 100, documents an anatomical mosaic; it does not by itself establish direct ancestry or a unique first bird.

title: Plumage color patterns of an extinct dinosaur
authors: Li, Q.; Gao, K.-Q.; Vinther, J.; et al.
note: Melanosome geometry and distribution in BMNHC PH828 support a statistical plumage-colour reconstruction; the tail was reconstructed from another specimen and exact colours are not direct observations.

title: Four-winged dinosaurs from China
authors: Xu, X.; Zhou, Z.; Wang, X.; Kuang, X.; Zhang, F.; Du, X.
note: IVPP V13352 preserves long pennaceous feathers on forelimbs, hindlimbs and tail; aerodynamic use and phylogenetic implications remain interpretations.

title: Aerodynamic performance of the feathered dinosaur Microraptor and the evolution of feathered flight
authors: Dyke, G.; de Kat, R.; Palmer, C.; van der Kindere, J.; Naish, D.; Ganapathisubramani, B.
note: A scaled physical model and wind-tunnel tests evaluate aerodynamic feasibility; model geometry and flow results are not observations of extinct behaviour.

title: Late Cretaceous neornithine from Europe illuminates the origins of crown birds
authors: Field, D.J.; Benito, J.; Chen, A.; Jagt, J.W.M.; Ksepka, D.T.
note: NHMM 2013 008 preserves a CT-imaged skull and postcrania near the K–Pg boundary; crown placement differs between parsimony and tip-dated analyses.

title: Whole-genome analyses resolve early branches in the tree of life of modern birds
authors: Jarvis, E.D.; Mirarab, S.; Aberer, A.J.; et al.
note: Genome-scale sampling of 48 species represents all neoavian orders then recognized; difficult branches and incomplete lineage sorting limit a single definitive topology.

title: A new time tree reveals Earth history's imprint on the evolution of modern birds
note: Fossil-calibrated Bayesian analyses combine clock-like exons and broader RAG sampling; divergence times and biogeographic histories are model outputs, not direct fossil observations.
